content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation source ledger.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-16 (apparatus 1-10, method 11-16), every entry in the numeral ledger (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140, 202-216), every structure, relationship, threshold, condition and stated result in the Field, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract, and every geometric and topological statement in the FIG. 1-4 briefs were checked against affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. Each substantive item traces to an exact affirmative passage: contactor/connector current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier per connector ("Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier"); branch sensor upstream of the contactors and treated as an independent safety input ("A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"; "The branch current sensor is an independent safety input"); isolated local bus reaching only interfaces and contactors ("communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus"), which matches the FIG. 1 bus not touching the non-charging load block and the FIG. 2 bus branching only to the contactor and the pilot interface; the four stored per-session values, the interval-by-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve, the sustaining-then-deficit assignment, pilot send and connector-sensor verification; the reduced pilot command, verification interval, and one-at-a-time ordered shedding "until measured branch current is below the branch limit" (which also supports claims 2 and 12 re-measuring between openings, and the claim 1/11 trigger via "staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond"); the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay (claims 3, 13); the leakage-threshold welded-contactor record, inhibition of the other contactors on the same branch, and local fault indicator (claims 4, 14); network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage behaviour, token expiry, and tamper-evident meter sequence (claims 6-8, 15); and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only after the sensed channel agrees (claims 9, 10, 16). Placement of the non-charging load 118 downstream of branch current sensor 104 traces to the disclosed subtraction of a "measured non-charging branch load" from the branch limit, and placement of connector current sensor 124 between contactor 122 and vehicle connector 128 traces to measurement of "a connector current delivered through that vehicle connector" combined with the branch sensor being upstream of the contactors. No untraced material, shape-substantive, proportion, count, contact-topology or flow-path assertion was found; the figure briefs confine their outline choices ("shown schematically") to the briefs, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" broadening appears in the application text. Numerals are one-to-one with parts, claim and description terminology agree, no section lines exist, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains. Abstract is 146 words. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to inventor sources, per instruction. One minor drawing-completeness inconsistency is reported: the description and claim 1 recite the controller being coupled to the connector current sensors, but the FIG. 2 detail view of connector channel 120 depicts no coupling for sensor 124. Note per the brief that no prior-art search was run, so the art available in prior_art/ may be incomplete; that does not bear on this source-fidelity result.

findings.title: Coupling of the controller to connector current sensor 124 is recited in claim 1 and the description but not depicted in the FIG. 2 detail view
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (connection paragraph and numeral list); draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph; draft/09-claims.md, claim 1 third element of the controller clause
findings.detail: Claim 1 requires "a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces ..., to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors ... and to the branch current sensor", and the description states "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." FIG. 2, which is the figure that breaks out the interior of connector channel 120, shows the isolated local bus 108 branching only "one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and a second upward to the contactor outline", and shows connector current sensor 124 as a circle straddling the power run with no signal path at all. The claimed and described coupling is therefore not shown in the detail view (37 CFR 1.83(a) requires every feature recited in the claims to be shown). The underlying coupling is itself source-supported, so this is a depiction gap rather than an unsupported assertion: the disclosure states the controller "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor", which requires a sensing path from the sensor to the controller. The fix must not attach the sensor to the isolated local bus, because the disclosure limits that bus to the interfaces and contactors: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus."
findings.evidence: Claim 1: "a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor". Description: "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." FIG-2.md: "A solid horizontal line enters from the left and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, as the isolated local bus. Inside the rectangle it branches two ways, one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and a second upward to the contactor outline." Source support for the coupling itself: disclosure, "The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, after the sentence describing the connector current sensor circle, add: "A separate solid line leaves the connector current sensor circle, runs left, and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle below the isolated local bus line, representing the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the measured connector current. This line does not join the isolated local bus line and crosses no other line work." Make no change to the claims or to the application text.
